title: Tensor products of tilde modules on an affine scheme
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $M,N$ be $R$-modules. Let $\widetilde M$, $\widetilde N$, $\widetilde{M\otimes_RN}$ be the $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], with canonical $R$-linear maps $\tau_M:M\to\widetilde M(X)$, $\tau_N:N\to\widetilde N(X)$, $\tau_{M\otimes N}:M\otimes_RN\to\widetilde{M\otimes_RN}(X)$. Let $\widetilde M\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\widetilde N$ be the tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], the sheafification of the presheaf $U\mapsto\widetilde M(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X(U)}\widetilde N(U)$, and for sections $a\in\widetilde M(U)$, $b\in\widetilde N(U)$ write $a\otimes b\in(\widetilde M\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\widetilde N)(U)$ for the image of $a\otimes b$ under the sheafification map. Then: (i) the map $\beta:M\otimes_RN\to(\widetilde M\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\widetilde N)(X)$, $m\otimes n\mapsto\tau_M(m)\otimes\tau_N(n)$, is a well-defined $R$-linear map, and there is a unique $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\alpha:\widetilde{M\otimes_RN}\to\widetilde M\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\widetilde N$ with $\alpha_X\circ\tau_{M\otimes N}=\beta$, i.e. $\alpha_X(\tau_{M\otimes N}(m\otimes n))=\tau_M(m)\otimes\tau_N(n)$ for all $m\in M$, $n\in N$ (the canonical map); (ii) $\alpha$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules; (iii) $\beta$ is bijective. This is Schemes, Lemma 01I8, item (1), with the map defined through the mapping property of Lemma 01I7.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I7 (lemma-compare-constructions) for the mapping property defining the map, and Lemma 01I8 (lemma-widetilde-constructions), item (1)

proof.text: Construction of $\beta$. Regard $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ of an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ as an $R$-module through $R=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, as in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. Write $P$ for the presheaf $U\mapsto\widetilde M(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X(U)}\widetilde N(U)$ and $t:P\to P^\#=\widetilde M\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\widetilde N$ for the sheafification map [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], which is $\mathcal O_X$-linear [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]; so $a\otimes b=t_X(a\otimes b)$ for $a\in\widetilde M(X)$, $b\in\widetilde N(X)$. The map $M\times N\to P^\#(X)$, $(m,n)\mapsto t_X(\tau_M(m)\otimes\tau_N(n))$, is $R$-bilinear: $\tau_M,\tau_N$ are $R$-linear, $(a,b)\mapsto a\otimes b$ is $\mathcal O_X(X)$-bilinear hence $R$-bilinear, and $t_X$ is $\mathcal O_X(X)$-linear. By the universal property of $M\otimes_RN$ it induces the $R$-linear map $\beta$ with $\beta(m\otimes n)=\tau_M(m)\otimes\tau_N(n)$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I8 (lemma-widetilde-constructions), second proof of part (1)

proof.text: Construction and uniqueness of $\alpha$ (Lemma 01I7: a map out of $\widetilde{M\otimes_RN}$ is the same as an $R$-linear map from $M\otimes_RN$ to global sections). By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (1), applied to the $R$-module $M\otimes_RN$ and the $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F=P^\#$, the map $\alpha\mapsto\alpha_X\circ\tau_{M\otimes N}$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\widetilde{M\otimes_RN},P^\#)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M\otimes_RN,P^\#(X))$. Let $\alpha$ be the preimage of $\beta$; then $\alpha_X(\tau_{M\otimes N}(m\otimes n))=\beta(m\otimes n)=\tau_M(m)\otimes\tau_N(n)$. If $\alpha'$ is another $\mathcal O_X$-linear map with $\alpha'_X(\tau_{M\otimes N}(m\otimes n))=\tau_M(m)\otimes\tau_N(n)$ for all $m,n$, then the $R$-linear maps $\alpha'_X\circ\tau_{M\otimes N}$ and $\beta$ agree on the generators $m\otimes n$ of $M\otimes_RN$, hence are equal, and injectivity of the bijection gives $\alpha'=\alpha$. This proves (i).

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I8, second proof of part (1), first sentence, using Lemma 01I7 (lemma-compare-constructions)

proof.text: Stalks at a point. Let $x\in X$ correspond to the prime $\mathfrak p$ and put $S=R\setminus\mathfrak p$ and $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$; the germ map $\rho:R\to A$ is a localization of $R$ at $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field] (1). The stalks $\widetilde M_x$, $\widetilde N_x$, $(\widetilde{M\otimes_RN})_x$, $P^\#_x$ are $A$-modules [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], regarded as $R$-modules via $\rho$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] the $R$-linear maps $\lambda_M:M\to\widetilde M_x$, $m\mapsto\tau_M(m)_x$, $\lambda_N:N\to\widetilde N_x$ and $\lambda_{M\otimes N}:M\otimes_RN\to(\widetilde{M\otimes_RN})_x$, $z\mapsto\tau_{M\otimes N}(z)_x$, are localizations at $S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product], applied to $\rho:R\to A$ and $\lambda_M,\lambda_N$, the $R$-linear map $u:M\otimes_RN\to\widetilde M_x\otimes_A\widetilde N_x$, $m\otimes n\mapsto\tau_M(m)_x\otimes\tau_N(n)_x$, is a localization of $M\otimes_RN$ at $S$ (this is the step 'tensor product commutes with localization', Algebra, Lemma 00DL, together with the description $\widetilde M_x=M_{\mathfrak p}$ of Schemes, Lemma 01HV (7)).

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I8 (lemma-widetilde-constructions), second proof of part (1)

proof.text: Comparison of the stalk map with $u$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-tensor] (Modules, Lemma 01CB) there is an $A$-linear isomorphism $\psi:P^\#_x\to\widetilde M_x\otimes_A\widetilde N_x$ with $\psi((a\otimes b)_x)=a_x\otimes b_x$ for sections $a,b$ over an open containing $x$. The stalk map $\alpha_x:(\widetilde{M\otimes_RN})_x\to P^\#_x$, $s_x\mapsto\alpha(s)_x$, is $A$-linear [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], so $h=\psi\circ\alpha_x$ is $A$-linear, hence $R$-linear. For $m\in M$, $n\in N$: $h(\lambda_{M\otimes N}(m\otimes n))=\psi(\alpha_X(\tau_{M\otimes N}(m\otimes n))_x)=\psi((\tau_M(m)\otimes\tau_N(n))_x)=\tau_M(m)_x\otimes\tau_N(n)_x=u(m\otimes n)$, using Step 2. Both $h\circ\lambda_{M\otimes N}$ and $u$ are $R$-linear and agree on the generators $m\otimes n$, so $h\circ\lambda_{M\otimes N}=u$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I8 (lemma-widetilde-constructions), second proof of part (1)

proof.text: $\alpha_x$ is bijective. Let $\ell_1=\lambda_{M\otimes N}:Q\to Q_1$ and $\ell_2=u:Q\to Q_2$ ($Q=M\otimes_RN$), both localizations of $Q$ at $S$ (Step 3), and $h:Q_1\to Q_2$ $R$-linear with $h\circ\ell_1=\ell_2$ (Step 4). Every $s\in S$ acts bijectively on $Q_1$ and $Q_2$ and $h$ commutes with $s$, hence with $s^{-1}$. Surjective: an element of $Q_2$ is $s^{-1}\ell_2(q)=h(s^{-1}\ell_1(q))$. Injective: an element of $Q_1$ is $s^{-1}\ell_1(q)$; if $h(s^{-1}\ell_1(q))=0$ then $\ell_2(q)=0$, so $s'q=0$ for some $s'\in S$, so $s'\ell_1(q)=0$ and $\ell_1(q)=0$ since $s'$ acts bijectively. Thus $h$ is bijective, and since $\psi$ is bijective, so is $\alpha_x=\psi^{-1}\circ h$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I8 (lemma-widetilde-constructions), second proof of part (1)

proof.text: $\alpha$ is an isomorphism. $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a scheme [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $\alpha$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules whose stalk map $\alpha_x$ is bijective at every $x\in X$ (Step 5); by [lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks] $\alpha$ is an isomorphism ('it suffices to check that it is an isomorphism on stalks'). This proves (ii).

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I8 (lemma-widetilde-constructions), second proof of part (1)

proof.text: Global sections. By Step 2, $\beta=\alpha_X\circ\tau_{M\otimes N}$. The unit $\tau_{M\otimes N}:M\otimes_RN\to\Gamma(X,\widetilde{M\otimes_RN})$ is bijective by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (2), and $\alpha_X$ is bijective because $\alpha$ is an isomorphism (Step 6; its inverse gives the inverse on sections over $X$). Hence $\beta$ is bijective, which is (iii).
